newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Arthuis pleased with rise in dollar.
newsitem.headline: France's Arthuis pleased with rise in dollar.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis told the cabinet on Wednesday he was pleased with the rise in the dollar with respect to the franc, government spokesman Alain Lamassoure said.

Arthuis said he was pleased "with developments in the foreign exchange markets, and in particular with the rise in the dollar, which at 5.80 francs these days explains in part our success in foreign trade," Lamassoure told reporters after the regular weekly cabinet meeting.
Arthuis made the statement during a report to the cabinet on last weekend's meeting of the Group of Seven industrialised nations in Washington.
Arthuis told the cabinet he was pleased above all at the G7 meeting by the positive reception given the prospect of the euro by France's G7 partners.

"It is already clear that the advent of the euro is viewed positively by our major partners as a central element of the international financial system of the future, and this is more and more being taken into account by the international financial community," Arthuis was quoted as saying.
Arthuis also expressed pleasure at the G7 meeting's positive assessment of the global financial outlook, and in particular at its rosy view of the outlook for the G7 nations themselves.
"Our own predictions of growth are confirmed, are in fact viewed as modest compared to the predicitions made by the international organisations," Arthuis said.

Finally, according to Lamassoure, Arthuis said he was pleased by International Monetary Fund and World Bank initiatives aimed at helping the poorest and most heavily indebted nations and in particular the Ivory Coast.
